title: Muhammad ﷺ is attested by outsiders within years of his death
thesis: Non-Muslim sources from the 630s-660s describe a prophet among the Arabs who preached the God of Abraham, forbade wine and fornication, and whose followers conquered Persia and Syria. That is the Muhammad of Islamic history, not a later invention.

premises.text: If Muhammad were a later legend, early non-Muslim witnesses should be silent or describe someone different.
Within a few decades of 632, Greek, Syriac and Armenian Christian sources, and then coins and inscriptions, name him and describe his message and movement in terms that match the Islamic sources.
Muhammad ﷺ is a firmly attested historical figure who taught what Islam says he taught.

evidence: Doctrina Jacobi (634): "a prophet has appeared among the Saracens".
Thomas the Presbyter (c. 640): mentions "the Arabs of Muhammad" (Mhmt, which some read as a title).
The Khuzistan Chronicle (c. 660): the Arabs led by MHMD conquered Persia.
Sebeos, Armenian bishop (c. 660s): Muhammad was a merchant who preached the God of Abraham, knew the Law of Moses, and forbade carrion, wine, lying and fornication.
Isho'yahb III, Catholicos of the Church of the East (c. 650s): the Arabs "are not only no enemy to Christianity, but are even praisers of our faith".

Physical evidence:
The Arab-Sasanian coins of Bishapur (66 AH) and later issues read "Muhammad is the messenger of God" in Pahlavi.
Abd al-Malik's dinars of the 70s AH carry the shahada.
The Hisma inscription, dated about 80 AH, reads "O God, bless Muhammad the Prophet".
The Syriac chronicle of the mid-8th century says Muhammad traded to Palestine.
Chinese sources: the Tang account and Du Huan (750s) describe the Arab religion, including prayer and a ban on wine .

objections.q: "The Islamic sources are too late; Muhammad might be a myth."
objections.a: The revisionists of the 1970s argued this, but they did not survive the evidence. Robert Hoyland (Seeing Islam as Others Saw It) collects dozens of non-Muslim witnesses within 150 years in six languages. Sinai's verdict above is now widely held.

practice.q: “Muhammad might be a later invention; the Islamic sources are late.”
practice.a: The Doctrina Jacobi (634) mentions a prophet among the Saracens; Sebeos (c. 660) describes him preaching the God of Abraham and forbidding wine and fornication; Isho'yahb III describes the Arabs. Sinai concludes a late-7th-century invention is improbable.

sum: Within thirty years of his death, Byzantine, Syriac and Armenian Christians were describing Muhammad ﷺ as a prophet of the God of Abraham who forbade wine and fornication. Coins and inscriptions confirm it, and Islamic history is corroborated by its rivals.
